back: The point through which the whole weight of an object can be taken to act.

front: Where is the centre of gravity of a regular uniform object?
back: At its geometric centre (it may be outside the material, e.g. a ring).

front: How do you find the centre of gravity of an irregular lamina?
back: Hang it freely, mark plumb-line verticals from two or more points; they cross at the centre of gravity.
When the line of action of its weight falls outside its base.
A low centre of gravity and a wide base.
Stable: returns after tilting. Unstable: falls over. Neutral: stays in the new position.

front: Why does a freely hanging object settle with its centre of gravity below the pivot?
back: Only then does its weight have no moment about the pivot.
